lookForward.fits: German Unity Day, a public holiday, is eight days away: Saturday 3 October 2026. Bremen hosts the official celebrations this year.
lookForward.headline: German Unity Day a week on Saturday
lookForward.line: 3 October, a holiday. The official party is in Bremen this year. Thirty-six years since two countries became one.

goodThing.fits: The cranes gathering over Brandenburg this week are a conservation success story for Germany.
goodThing.headline: Germany's cranes came back
goodThing.line: Down to about 800 breeding pairs in the 1970s. Wetlands were protected and hunting stopped. Now they fill the September sky.

onThisDay.headline: Germany's rulers agreed to disagree about God
onThisDay.line: The Peace of Augsburg. For the first time, two Christian faiths were legal side by side in one empire.

funFact.fits: Everyday German life: the deposit system every reader in Germany uses.
funFact.statement: In Germany, almost every bottle and can you buy comes with money on it.
funFact.reveal: A deposit of 25 cents since 2003. About 98 in every 100 come back to the shop and are recycled.
more: Germany’s deposit system began in 2003, when a law made shops charge a deposit on most single-use drinks containers. Since 2006 it has been a flat 25 cents on cans and plastic bottles, and since 2022 it covers almost everything, including juice and milk. Reusable glass bottles carry a smaller deposit, 8 or 15 cents, and go back to the brewery to be washed and refilled up to fifty times.

The return rate for single-use containers is around 98 percent, one of the highest in the world. The machines in every supermarket read the barcode and the deposit logo, crush the container, and print a voucher. The material is recycled: a plastic bottle becomes a plastic bottle again.

The side effect nobody planned is the small economy of collecting. Because a bottle is worth money, people leave empties standing beside bins rather than in them, and other people collect them. In some cities there are Pfandringe, rings fixed to bins where bottles can be placed so nobody has to reach inside. It is not a solution to poverty, but it is a kind of manners.

word.meaning: The moment work ends and the evening is yours. Once the evening before a holy day; now every evening, and on Fridays said with feeling.

kindness.text: It's Friday. Leave on time, and take someone with you who never does.

joke.setup: What do you call a German who leaves work at four on a Friday?

riddle.fits: The deposit system in today's fun fact.
riddle.riddle: I am worth 25 cents, I am not a coin, and I live under your sink. What am I?
riddle.hint: Take me back to the shop.
riddle.answer: An empty bottle with a deposit on it.
